claims.statement: Each catalog-authored and persisted Schedule requires a supported skip or run_once policy and an explicit integer grace from zero through one day. Policy and grace survive file-backed SQLite restart, participate in exact replay and the full consistency digest, and have portable schema and database constraints so missing, fractional, out-of-range, or unsealed changed values fail closed.

Misfire classification uses only the immutable persisted due instant and committed claim time: equality with due plus grace remains on time and only a strictly later claim is a misfire. The planner reads no processing clock, validates the complete schedule and claim snapshot, and rejects inconsistent identities, due times, recurrence versions, fencing versions, and recurrence outputs.

A skip misfire produces one immutable no-work intent anchored to the original persisted due instant, with the first missed instant, last coalesced instant, exact count, and first recurrence strictly after claim time. Enumeration has a hard safe ceiling and fails closed rather than truncating a long outage or emitting a backlog.

A run_once misfire coalesces every recurrence through claim time into one work-admission intent anchored to the originally persisted due instant, retains the exact bounded missed range, and selects the first strictly future wall-clock occurrence. It returns one plan rather than one intent per missed recurrence.

limitations: SCHED-02 owns exclusive lease acquisition, and SCHED-03 owns stable occurrence identity plus normal Work and Run ingress. SCHED-04 consumes an exact already-issued claim and does not replace either boundary.

SCHED-04 produces a pure immutable policy intent and performs no unit-of-work mutation. SCHED-05 owns the live claim fence, authoritative skipped or catch-up occurrence persistence, optional Work and Run receipt, audit, next-time advancement, lease release, and single atomic commit.

No-work and one-catch-up behavior are planner directives here, not claims about committed WorkItem or Run row counts. Those database side effects and rollback fault injection remain SCHED-05 evidence.
SCHED-06 retains expired-lease discovery, restart recovery races, and duplicate suppression after lease recovery.
The missed-range algorithm coalesces at most 10000 occurrences and fails closed when that bound is exceeded; it does not claim unlimited historical catch-up.
Stable catch-up identity remains anchored to the persisted original due instant, not claim or processing time. A recovered later claim may safely calculate a wider uncommitted range.

V1 remains five-field cron with the existing IANA timezone, spring-gap, and fold-zero policy. Timezone-database updates may affect newly calculated future projections but not prior stable occurrence IDs.

Runtime persistence evidence uses file-backed SQLite. PostgreSQL table and constraint DDL compile, but PostgreSQL runtime contention, migrations, audit, metrics, polling, APIs, authorization, deployment, and exactly-once Run execution remain outside scope.
